newsitem.title: USA: White House hails deal between NATO and Russia.
newsitem.headline: White House hails deal between NATO and Russia.

text.p: The White House on Wednesday applauded the news that NATO and Russia had agreed on terms of peaceful new relationship, and said it could result in a Paris signing ceremony later this month.

"We're obviously very encouraged," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters. He said the prospective agreement was something that President Bill Clinton had fought for and worked hard on "for quite some time."

The text of the deal was agreed to at talks in Moscow between Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and NATO Secretary General Javier Solana after months of tough negotiations between the two former Cold War foes.

"The president at Helsinki cleared the way for a lot of the issues that needed to be discussed," McCurry said, referring to Clinton's summit with Russian President Boris Yeltsin in the Finnish capital in March.

McCurry said Solana was expected to brief NATO representatives on details of the agreement at noon Washington time (1600 GMT), and that Clinton was likely to make a public statement about the pact on Thursday afternoon.

"It's looking likely if they can finalize this agreement that there would be a signing ceremony in Paris that President Yeltsin suggested occur," McCurry said. Yeltsin has set a target date of May 27 for a Paris big power summit to sign the agreement.
